evidence: the-lock-wait-is-bounded: puppet_boot_run.sh:5 sets LOCK_WAIT_MAX=120 and :25-29 log 'Apt/dpkg locks still present after ${LOCK_WAIT_MAX}s; continuing anyway.' then break; with lock-frontend held 150 s the probe expects exactly that log line once and the 'Running puppet agent at' timestamp >= start+120 and < the release time, which is what the bounded loop (3 s polls, then line 35 of the current file) produces; relies on local change #13 (lsof -t) for the wait to happen at all

the-unit-makes-an-agent-run: puppet_boot_run.sh:33-42 log 'Running puppet agent at', run 'timeout 900 puppet agent -t' into the log and exit 0; the effect checks unit start rc=0 and Result=success (oneshot, script always exits 0), one Running line, one 'Notice: Applied catalog in' line from puppet agent -t, last_run_summary newer than the start, and (lines 19-31) that the agent run started only after the 15 s dpkg lock-frontend hold was released (the release stamp is written before the holder's fd closes, so ran >= released is sound)

script-and-unit-installed: service.erb:5-7 render [Service] Type=oneshot and ExecStart=<%= @boot_run_script %>, which the manifest (lines 8-9) sets to lookup('filesystem::bindir')/puppet_boot_run.sh = /opt/puppet-infrastructure/bin/puppet_boot_run.sh; manifest 11-17 give root:root 0750 from the module file, whose current sha256 99b6e01a...a66b I computed from files/etc/puppet_boot_run.sh (baseline + local change #13); unit file 0644 root root and WantedBy=multi-user.target (erb:11) match

purpose covered: Purpose (one agent run per boot via a oneshot unit wanted by multi-user.target, with lock wait, skip-if-running and a time limit) matches the class header and baseline manifest/script/template. Checks test the unit installed and enabled/wanted by multi-user.target, the skip path with the agent lockfile present (start succeeds, Skipping logged, no agent run), the dpkg-lock wait followed by a real agent run that applies the catalog and updates last_run_summary, and the 120 s bound on the lock wait. Uncovered rows are honest: the 900 s PUPPET_TIMEOUT cut-off exceeds the runner's 1-600 s mutating-action timeout (phase3.py:522-523), and a real boot/After=network.target ordering needs a reboot step phase3.py lacks (revert, apply, probe, node_agent only); both lifted by capabilities, not an active node kind. Left out without a row: the else branch for a node without the timeout binary (coreutils always present on Ubuntu 24.04) and 'not kept running' is shown by the harness's clean second run rather than a probe; neither is a lab-exercisable gap in the purpose.
